A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Early Cutting research work and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Relocated material, including the detailed settings and CIFAR-100 figure panels, can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V2 reports original Early Cutting benchmark results, controlled experiments on mislabeled examples, sensitivity analyses, and component ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds influence-function results and feature-space analyses at later training epochs.

M1.justification: The filtering components and thresholds are retained. However, Algorithm 1 switches from v2's three-consecutive-epoch learning-time rule in Eq. (13) to the two-epoch rule in Eq. (1), while v3 Appendix D.5 still specifies three epochs. Whether this represents an intended procedural change or an inconsistent cross-reference is unresolved.

E1.justification: The evaluated image-classification datasets and noise scenarios are retained, including Fashion-MNIST and the TinyViT experiment already present in v2 Table 10. New analyses reuse CIFAR settings; Appendix C's NLP and regression examples are conceptual, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons in Tables 1–6, 8, and 10 retain their comparator membership, including VOG, CSGN, and the semi-supervised baselines. V3 clarifies supervised-only use of CSGN without establishing a change to the evaluated variant.

E3.justification: New Appendix B introduces influence-score evaluation against clean held-out validation data, comparing three cohorts of 4,000 examples each. Appendix E adds feature-space evaluations at epochs 40 and 160. The retained benchmark split, noise-rate, architecture, and training-budget descriptions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds a focused influence-function analysis of individual-example harm and a longitudinal extension of the feature-space analysis. Figure 4(a) is also revised. Existing component ablations, sensitivity tests, pretraining checks, and transferability studies are retained, including relocated CIFAR-100 panels.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 newly specifies that results reported as mean±standard deviation summarize three trials with different random seeds. V2 already reported these uncertainty summaries but omitted the trial count and seed information; an increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: Appendix B adds mean influence scores of 4.96 for MEEs, 3.01 for mislabeled hard examples, and -2.22 for clean easy examples. Figure 4(a)'s plotted distributions change, and Figure 8 adds later-epoch results. Tables 1–10 retain their numerical results apart from equivalent formatting such as 65.1 versus 65.10.

T1.justification: Operational Definition 1 combines the filtering conditions already expressed by v2's Eqs. (3) and (5). Appendix A clarifies random-variable notation without changing the mathematical relationships. No new substantive derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims that early-learned mislabeled examples disproportionately harm generalization and that later-state recalibration can filter them effectively. The added analyses support these existing contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands applicability and limitations discussion. Section 5 explicitly addresses visual-only validation, observational justification, computational overhead, and possible minority-class filtering under severe noise or imbalance. Appendix C discusses conceptual NLP and regression adaptations, while Section 2.1 refines the interpretation of the pretraining check as evidence of learning ease.

D1.justification: V3 adds an implementation link, identifies the influence-function library, and discloses validation-based threshold selection. It also specifies that MixMatch's labeled/unlabeled partition stays fixed and clarifies supervised-only CSGN evaluation. These are additional reproducibility disclosures, not evidence that the retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations for influence functions, SAM, Jacobian sensitivity, and TinyViT, while removing several general label-noise references. Appendix A expands connections to gradient-based difficulty and input sensitivity; the principal positioning relative to existing sample-selection methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 2.1 is condensed, notation and pseudocode are clarified, and contributions receive list formatting. Algorithm 1 moves into the main text, existing settings move from Appendix B to D, and new appendices and acknowledgments are inserted. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a document-wide NeurIPS layout with changed typography, title treatment, and text width. Algorithm 1 moves into the main text; v2 Figures 2(b) and 3(b) become appendix Figures 6 and 7. Figure 4(a) is redrawn, Figure 8 is added, and tables and figures are extensively reflowed.

improvement.justification: The added influence and temporal analyses provide useful supporting evidence, while the trial-count disclosure, implementation link, and specific limitations improve transparency. These gains are incremental: benchmark scores remain unchanged, and the learning-time inconsistency and vaguely specified component-ablation setting remain unresolved.
